secret_gate_second_blind_spot.what: The home-path rule matches an account name inside a path. It does not match the name standing on its own, and the repository had published it that way six times while the rule reported two: pytest-of-<name> in a host note in this file and in STATE.md, and account='<name>' four times in the evidence file that documented the first leak.
secret_gate_second_blind_spot.how_it_surfaced: node scripts/qa_secrets.mjs failed at HEAD on .kodro/ca2-evidence/2026-08-15-secret-gate-utf16-blind-spot.md:22 and :46. Those two lines were path-shaped so the existing rule caught them. A repo-wide git grep for the account token then found six more that it could not see.
secret_gate_second_blind_spot.redaction: All eight occurrences across four tracked files replaced with <account>: the evidence file (4), this file (2), .kodro/autonomy/STATE.md (1, the pytest temp-root note), and the evidence file's measurement lines. The measurements themselves are unchanged: 20 HOME_PATH matches under utf16le against 0 under utf8 still reads exactly as it was taken. Only the disclosed value is gone.
secret_gate_second_blind_spot.rule_added: A bare-name rule in scripts/qa_secrets.mjs. A bare name has no shape to match, so it is matched by value: the account running the scan, read from os.userInfo() at run time so the gate never stores a name. Guarded on alphanumerics rather than \b so pytest-of-<name> is caught while a longer word merely containing the name is not. Names shorter than four characters and shared CI accounts are declined.
secret_gate_second_blind_spot.honest_limit: This is a publisher-side check, not a universal one. It catches the leak the machine running it can create, which is the only one it is in a position to prevent. It is inactive when there is no usable local account name, so the PASS line now states 'bare-name rule live' or 'bare-name rule inactive' rather than letting a green line imply a check that did not run.

site_dir_collision.how_it_surfaced: node scripts/qa_web.mjs came back 2 of 5 with 'FAIL privacy-zero-external LEAKED to: api.github.com'. Kodro Web makes zero external requests by design, so the honest move was to check the premise before reporting a privacy regression.
site_dir_collision.what_site_actually_contained: The MkDocs documentation site, not the Kodro Web static build. The api.github.com request was Material for MkDocs fetching the repository star count. The product was never leaking; the gate was measuring the wrong directory.
site_dir_collision.the_real_defect: docs/mkdocs.yml declared site_dir: ../site. That is the same directory scripts/build_web.cjs --static writes the Kodro Web static build to and that scripts/qa_web.mjs reads (const SITE = path.join(ROOT, 'site')). Two tools owned one output directory, and qa_web.mjs reads it without building it, so it measures whatever wrote there last. A `mkdocs build` in between makes the product's own privacy gate measure the documentation site instead. That is not hypothetical: it is what produced the api.github.com report above.
site_dir_collision.what_it_could_NOT_do: It could not have shipped the documentation site to GitHub Pages, and an earlier draft of this entry claimed it could. Checked rather than assumed: .github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml runs `node scripts/build_web.cjs --static` at line 43 and uploads `path: site` at line 49, in a fresh checkout on a fresh runner, so site/ is always rebuilt immediately before upload. ci.yml does the same inside the qa_web step itself. The blast radius is local working copies, which is where it went off. Recording the correction because overstating a defect is the same reporting failure as understating one.
site_dir_collision.why_it_had_never_fired: The documentation build had never been run in CI or in any gate matrix. It was added as a gate on 15 August (see docs_build_gated_for_the_first_time), which is the same change that would have made this collision fire on every CI run on main.
site_dir_collision.fix: docs/mkdocs.yml now uses site_dir: ../.docs-site, with the reason written at the setting so nobody moves it back. .gitignore gains .docs-site/ and an explanatory comment on site/. The docs gate in ci.yml carries the same explanation and is ordered before the web gates.
